project.name: SETURA
project.description: Multi-tenant hospital operations platform — all business logic in PostgreSQL (SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, triggers, constraints); Deno edge functions provide authorized HTTP APIs, orchestration, and notification side-effects. No application-side state.

nodes.name: auth.ts
nodes.summary: Central authentication and authorization module for all Edge Functions. Extracts JWTs, resolves user roles from profiles and user_roles, enforces role hierarchy, and provides withAuth wrapper for request-level auth. Supports hospital-scoped access control and global admin bypass.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Supabase Auth client for JWT verification and service-role client for privileged profile lookups. ROLE_HIERARCHY defines precedence: global_admin > hospital_admin > doctor > receptionist > patient.

nodes.name: errors.ts
nodes.summary: Comprehensive domain error hierarchy for SETURA. Defines 18 error classes extending SeturError base class, covering auth, booking, queue, idempotency, rate limiting, and infrastructure failures. No dependencies — pure domain error definitions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript class inheritance with code, statusCode, retryable flag, and optional context. isSeturError and isRetryable are type guards used by handleErrorResponse.

nodes.name: rate_limit.ts
nodes.summary: Booking attempt rate limiting and blocklist checking. Enforces per-phone and per-IP rate limit windows, checks blocked_numbers table, and logs all attempts. Used by create-booking to prevent abuse.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses blocked_numbers table for patient blocklist and booking_attempt_logs for rate tracking. Configurable windows via Env config.

nodes.name: response.ts
nodes.summary: Standardized API response builders for all Edge Functions. Provides success, created, error, and typed error response helpers with consistent JSON envelope (success flag, correlationId, timestamp). Injects CORS headers on all responses.
nodes.languageNotes: All responses follow ApiSuccessResponse or ApiErrorResponse envelope. handleErrorResponse is the outermost catch-block handler for all endpoints.

nodes.name: validation.ts
nodes.summary: Request validation helpers: Zod schemas for common types (UUID, phone, date, gender, blood group, booking source) and request body parsing with field-level error aggregation.

nodes.name: reporting.ts
nodes.summary: Report data transformation utilities for CSV and PDF-ready export formats. Flattens nested report objects to dot-notation keys, escapes CSV values, and formats data for PDF generation.

nodes.name: setup_env.ts
nodes.summary: Test environment setup utility. Configures test environment variables (CORS origins, Supabase URLs/keys) for integration and unit test execution.

nodes.name: extractJwt
nodes.summary: Extracts and parses Bearer token from Authorization header.

nodes.name: selectRole
nodes.summary: Selects the highest-privilege role from user_roles rows based on ROLE_HIERARCHY scope. Resolves primary vs secondary roles, logs warnings on ambiguity.

nodes.name: resolveAuth
nodes.summary: Core auth resolver. Verifies JWT via Supabase Auth, loads user profile, queries user_roles for hospital membership and role, handles global admin bypass. Returns full AuthContext used by all handlers.

nodes.name: requireRole
nodes.summary: Enforces that the authenticated user has at least one of the required roles. Throws RoleInsufficientError if not.

nodes.name: requireHospitalAccess
nodes.summary: Ensures the authenticated user is a member of the target hospital. Throws HospitalAccessDeniedError if not.

nodes.name: isGlobalAdmin
nodes.summary: Returns true if the auth context has global_admin role.

nodes.name: hasRole
nodes.summary: Checks if the auth context has a specific role.

nodes.name: canManageQueue
nodes.summary: Returns true if the user can manage queue operations (hospital_admin, doctor, receptionist).

nodes.name: canViewAnalytics
nodes.summary: Returns true if the user can view analytics (hospital_admin, global_admin).

nodes.name: withAuth
nodes.summary: Higher-order handler wrapper that runs resolveAuth and requireRole on every request before delegating to the actual handler. Applies CORS and generates correlationId.

nodes.name: SeturError
nodes.summary: Base error class for all SETURA domain errors. Carries code, HTTP status code, retryable flag, optional context, and ISO timestamp. Implements toJSON for serialization.

nodes.name: UnauthorizedError
nodes.summary: 401 Unauthorized — no valid JWT or session expired.

nodes.name: ForbiddenError
nodes.summary: 403 Forbidden — authenticated but insufficient privileges.

nodes.name: HospitalAccessDeniedError
nodes.summary: 403 — user does not belong to the target hospital (multi-tenancy boundary violation).

nodes.name: RoleInsufficientError
nodes.summary: 403 — user lacks required role. Reports which roles were required vs what user has.

nodes.name: ValidationError
nodes.summary: 422 — request body failed schema validation. Carries fieldErrors map.

nodes.name: BookingDuplicateError
nodes.summary: 409 — duplicate booking detected (same patient, doctor, date/slot).

nodes.name: HospitalClosedError
nodes.summary: 403 — operation attempted outside hospital operating hours.

nodes.name: QueueFullError
nodes.summary: 403 — queue has reached its maximum capacity.

nodes.name: TokenExhaustedError
nodes.summary: 403 — doctor has issued all allocated tokens for the session.

nodes.name: DoctorUnavailableError
nodes.summary: 404 — doctor not found or not active for the requested hospital.

nodes.name: PatientBlockedError
nodes.summary: 403 — patient phone is on the hospital blocklist or restricted list.

nodes.name: IdempotencyKeyRequiredError
nodes.summary: 400 — mutation endpoint called without required idempotency key header.

nodes.name: IdempotencyProcessingError
nodes.summary: 409 — idempotency key already claimed by an in-flight request (retry race).

nodes.name: RateLimitError
nodes.summary: 429 — too many booking attempts from the same phone or IP within a time window.

nodes.name: ConcurrencyError
nodes.summary: 409 — concurrent modification detected (race condition in optimistic concurrency).

nodes.name: DbError
nodes.summary: 500 — database operation failed unexpectedly.

nodes.name: InternalError
nodes.summary: 500 — unexpected internal error with optional context.

nodes.name: isSeturError
nodes.summary: Type guard — returns true if the value is a SeturError instance.

nodes.name: isRetryable
nodes.summary: Returns true if the error is retryable (marked with retryable: true).

nodes.name: checkAndLogBookingAttempt
nodes.summary: Core rate limit gate. Normalizes phone, checks blocked_numbers table for active restriction, counts attempts in current window, throws RateLimitError or PatientBlockedError if exceeded, and logs all attempts.

nodes.name: extractIp
nodes.summary: Extracts client IP from X-Forwarded-For or socket address.

nodes.name: successResponse
nodes.summary: 200 OK response with ApiSuccessResponse envelope (success: true, data, correlationId, timestamp, optional meta).

nodes.name: createdResponse
nodes.summary: 201 Created response — delegates to successResponse with status 201.

nodes.name: errorResponse
nodes.summary: Generic error response builder. ApiErrorResponse envelope with code, message, optional fieldErrors, retryable flag, correlationId, timestamp.

nodes.name: fromSeturError
nodes.summary: Converts a domain SeturError to an HTTP response using the error's code, statusCode, retryable flag, and fieldErrors.

nodes.name: unauthorizedResponse
nodes.summary: 401 Unauthorized with code UNAUTHORIZED.

nodes.name: forbiddenResponse
nodes.summary: 403 Forbidden with code FORBIDDEN.

nodes.name: validationErrorResponse
nodes.summary: 422 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and fieldErrors map.

nodes.name: conflictResponse
nodes.summary: 409 Conflict with a caller-supplied code and message.

nodes.name: rateLimitResponse
nodes.summary: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header. Body has retryable: true.

nodes.name: internalErrorResponse
nodes.summary: 500 Internal Server Error with code INTERNAL_ERROR.

nodes.name: handleErrorResponse
nodes.summary: Outer catch-block handler: routes SeturError instances via fromSeturError, everything else to internalErrorResponse.

nodes.name: normalizePhone
nodes.summary: Normalizes phone number: strips non-digits, ensures starts with country code.

nodes.name: parseBody
nodes.summary: Parses JSON request body through a Zod schema, returns parsed data or throws ValidationError with fieldErrors map keyed by dot-notation path.

nodes.name: isValidAdvanceBookingDate
nodes.summary: Checks whether a booking date is within the allowed advance window (today to today + maxAdvanceDays).

nodes.name: getWeekday
nodes.summary: Returns the day of week for a date string (0=Sunday, 6=Saturday).

nodes.name: flattenObject
nodes.summary: Recursively flattens nested objects into dot-notation keys (e.g. patient.name -> patient_name). Handles arrays by JSON stringifying.

nodes.name: reportToCsv
nodes.summary: Converts a report (array of objects or single object with rows/data) into RFC-4180-compliant CSV. Automatically flattens nested objects and unions all column keys.

nodes.name: reportToPdfReady
nodes.summary: Converts report data to PDF-ready format: flattens objects, converts values to strings, adds timestamp.

nodes.name: enterprise-reports/index.ts
nodes.summary: Enterprise report generation Edge Function. Supports multi-hospital reporting, date-range filters, CSV and PDF export formats via the reporting module.

nodes.name: executive-analytics/index.ts
nodes.summary: Executive dashboard analytics Edge Function. Aggregates high-level KPIs (bookings, revenue, queue health) across the hospital for executive and admin consumption.

nodes.name: financial-command-center/index.ts
nodes.summary: Financial operations command center. Provides aggregated financial views, collection summaries, and settlement status for hospital finance teams.

nodes.languageNotes: Thin orchestration layer over queue_runtime.ts — routes action parameter to the appropriate run* function.

nodes.name: refresh-rollups/index.ts
nodes.summary: Refreshes pre-computed analytics rollup tables. Triggered by cron or manually. Recomputes daily/weekly/monthly aggregations for dashboard performance.

nodes.name: audit.ts
nodes.summary: Provides fire-and-forget audit event writing to the audit_logs table via write_audit_log RPC. Enforces that governance events never silently disappear by coercing non-UUID entity/actor references into data fields, reading PostgREST errors explicitly, and reporting failures to logger and metrics.

nodes.name: logAuditEvent
nodes.summary: Writes a structured audit event to audit_logs via write_audit_log RPC. Never throws; returns AuditWriteOutcome so callers can react to failures. Relocates non-UUID entityId/actorUserId into newData.entityRef/newData.actorRef to preserve the reference while satisfying UUID column constraints.

nodes.name: isUuid

nodes.name: whatsapp_booking_flow.ts
nodes.summary: WhatsApp booking flow: patient identified, doctor selected, date validated, booking confirmed. State machine with steps: name, doctor, date, confirm. Delegates booking creation to the atomic create_booking RPC to avoid duplicating allocation, fee lookup, and availability logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Stateful flow using BookingFlowState with step-based progression. Reuses is_doctor_available RPC, get_effective_fees RPC, hospital holiday/working-hours checks, and the canonical create_booking RPC.

nodes.name: startBookingFlow
nodes.summary: Entry point when a booking intent arrives outside an active flow. Captures date hints from the initial message, resolves or creates the patient, and begins the doctor-selection step.

nodes.name: continueBookingFlow
nodes.summary: Advances an in-progress booking flow based on the current state (booking, selecting_doctor, selecting_date, confirming). Handles retries up to MAX_STEP_RETRIES (3) before escalating to human handoff. Executes booking via create_booking RPC with idempotency key.

nodes.name: listActiveDoctors
nodes.summary: Queries doctor_schedules for active doctors at a hospital, deduplicates, and resolves full names from profiles. Returns an array of {id, name}.

nodes.name: validateAppointmentDate
nodes.summary: Validates a requested appointment date against the hospital booking window, holidays, working hours, and doctor availability (via is_doctor_available RPC). Returns a patient-facing error message or null if valid.

nodes.name: whatsapp_cancel_flow.ts
nodes.summary: WhatsApp cancellation flow: finds the nearest cancellable booking for a phone, prompts for confirmation, cancels with optimistic status guard, and initiates a partial refund per the hospital cancellation policy.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses initiate_refund RPC for fee refunds and recalculate_queue_position RPC to update the queue after cancellation.

nodes.name: startCancelFlow
nodes.summary: Entry point for the cancel intent. Finds the nearest cancellable booking for the patient phone and prompts for confirmation with booking details.

nodes.name: continueCancelFlow
nodes.summary: Handles confirmation reply (yes/no) for a pending cancellation. Calls executeCancel on yes; escalates to handoff after MAX_STEP_RETRIES failures.

nodes.name: whatsapp_conversation_engine.ts
nodes.summary: Central orchestrator for the WhatsApp-first patient experience. Consumes one inbound message, resolves intent via classifyIntent, manages hospital-scoped/phone-scoped conversation state via get_conversation_state/set_conversation_state RPCs, dispatches to flow modules, and enqueues reply jobs through enqueue_job. No LLM intent routing; deterministic keyword matching only.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports FlowContext, FlowResult, ConversationStateName, HospitalWaConfig types consumed by all flow modules. State machine prevents conversations from getting stuck via handoff escalation.

nodes.name: processInboundMessage
nodes.summary: Main entry point: idempotently records the inbound message, checks the whatsapp_conversation feature flag, loads conversation state, classifies intent, dispatches to the appropriate flow, persists state and enqueues replies as send_whatsapp_message jobs.

nodes.name: loadHospitalWaConfig
nodes.summary: Loads per-hospital WhatsApp configuration (display name, greeting, queue wording, max advance booking days) from hospital_settings and hospitals tables.

nodes.name: enqueueReplies
nodes.summary: Enqueues one send_whatsapp_message job per reply text via enqueue_job RPC, using the meta message ID as an idempotency key.

nodes.name: persistState
nodes.summary: Persists conversation state and unknown-intent count to the database via set_conversation_state RPC, including the handoff reason when transitioning to handoff state.

nodes.name: fill
nodes.summary: Simple {placeholder} string interpolation for hospital-configurable greeting/queue wording templates.

nodes.name: whatsapp_handoff_flow.ts
nodes.summary: Human handoff flow: escalates a WhatsApp conversation to hospital staff when the patient asks, when intents repeatedly fail, or when a flow errors. Conversations must never get stuck. Exports WA_PATIENT_ACTOR constant used in WhatsApp audit attribution.

nodes.name: escalateToHandoff
nodes.summary: Transitions the conversation to handoff state with a reason (patient_requested, repeated_unknown_intent, repeated_flow_failure, flow_error) and returns the standard handoff reply.

nodes.name: whatsapp_intent_router.ts
nodes.summary: Deterministic keyword-based intent classification for WhatsApp messages: book, queue_status, reschedule, cancel, yes, no, handoff, help, greeting, unknown. No LLM. Also exports date parsing (today, tomorrow, weekdays, dd/mm formats) and patient name / choice extraction.
nodes.languageNotes: IST-friendly date parsing supports Telugu keywords (eroju, repu) alongside English. Intent precedence order prevents misclassification.

nodes.name: classifyIntent
nodes.summary: Classifies a raw message into exactly one Intent using ordered keyword matching. Precedence: reschedule > cancel > book > queue > handoff > help > greeting > yes/no (weakest).

nodes.name: parseDateInput
nodes.summary: Parses relative and absolute date phrases into YYYY-MM-DD. Supports today, tomorrow, day-after-tomorrow, weekday names, dd/mm, dd-mm, dd/mm/yyyy. Rolls bare dd/mm past dates into next year.

nodes.name: normalizeText
nodes.summary: Normalizes free text for deterministic matching: lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace.

nodes.name: extractName
nodes.summary: Extracts a patient name from phrases like 'my name is X' in multiple languages (English, Telugu patterns).

nodes.name: extractChoice
nodes.summary: Extracts a numeric choice (1-20) from doctor menu replies, matching 'option N', 'doctor N', 'N', or 'no N' patterns.

nodes.name: whatsapp_queue_flow.ts
nodes.summary: Read-only WhatsApp queue status lookup: returns the patient's token, current live token, patients ahead, and estimated wait time. Sanitizes phone input to prevent PostgREST filter injection. Uses queue_sessions and doctor_schedules tables for live data.
nodes.languageNotes: sanitizePhone() is a defensive injection guard: strips all non-digit/+ characters and validates E.164-like shape before the phone enters a PostgREST .or() filter string.

nodes.name: handleQueueLookup
nodes.summary: Handles the queue_status intent: finds today's booking for the phone, looks up the current live token from queue_sessions, computes patients ahead, estimates wait time using doctor's average consultation minutes, and returns status-appropriate replies.

nodes.name: whatsapp_reschedule_flow.ts
nodes.summary: WhatsApp reschedule flow: finds the nearest reschedulable booking, validates the new date, marks the old booking as rescheduled with an optimistic guard, and creates a new booking via the atomic create_booking RPC. Links new booking to the original via carry_forwarded_from.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the same date validation (validateAppointmentDate) and booking creation RPC as the reschedule-booking REST endpoint, avoiding logic duplication.

nodes.name: startRescheduleFlow
nodes.summary: Entry point for the reschedule intent. Finds the nearest reschedulable booking, pre-populates the date if one was mentioned in the message, and prompts for a new date.

nodes.name: continueRescheduleFlow
nodes.summary: Advances a reschedule flow: handles date input or confirmation (yes/no). Escalates to handoff after MAX_STEP_RETRIES failures.

nodes.name: executeReschedule
nodes.summary: Executes the reschedule: marks old booking as rescheduled (with optimistic status guard), creates new booking via create_booking RPC with carry_forwarded_from link, and logs audit event.

nodes.name: handleNewDate
nodes.summary: Validates a new date and prompts for confirmation. Rejects same-day reschedules and validates against hospital holidays, working hours, and doctor availability.

nodes.name: 01_foundation.sql
nodes.summary: SETURA foundation migration: creates core enums (user_role_type, booking_status, booking_source), helper functions (set_updated_at, prevent_hospital_id_update), and core tables (hospitals, profiles, user_roles, patients, hospital_working_hours, hospital_holidays) with RLS policies. Establishes SECURITY DEFINER auth helpers (current_user_role, is_global_admin, user_has_hospital_access, user_has_hospital_role).
nodes.languageNotes: PostgreSQL with SECURITY DEFINER functions, RLS policies, trigger functions, and CHECK constraints for multi-tenancy.

nodes.name: 02_atomic_token_engine_&_bookings.sql
nodes.summary: Atomic token engine and bookings: creates hospital_daily_counters table, generate_next_token() SECURITY DEFINER function, queue_sessions table, bookings table with full booking lifecycle, booking_events audit table. Includes handle_booking_status_change trigger, create_booking() and advance_queue() RPCs. Adds Realtime publication for bookings/booking_events/queue_sessions.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic upsert pattern for token generation using ON CONFLICT. Concurrency-safe queue advancement using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

nodes.name: 03_doctorscheduling&slotengine.sql
nodes.summary: Doctor scheduling and slot engine: creates doctor_specializations, doctor_schedules (with btree_gist exclusion constraint for no-overlapping schedules), doctor_schedule_blocks, doctor_leaves (with daterange exclusion), override_type enum, and doctor_availability_overrides tables. Provides is_doctor_available(), get_remaining_token_capacity(), estimate_wait_minutes() SECURITY DEFINER functions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PostgreSQL exclusion constraints with btree_gist extension for schedule conflict prevention.

nodes.name: 04_whatsapp_messaging_engine.sql
nodes.summary: WhatsApp messaging engine: creates whatsapp_message_status/direction/template_category enums, whatsapp_templates, whatsapp_conversations, whatsapp_messages, whatsapp_delivery_logs, and whatsapp_webhook_events tables. Provides find_or_create_whatsapp_conversation(), queue_whatsapp_message(), fetch_pending_whatsapp_messages(), handle_whatsapp_delivery_status(), schedule_whatsapp_retry(), register_webhook_event() SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
nodes.languageNotes: WhatsApp message status state machine with retry logic (exponential backoff capped at 1440 mins). Idempotent webhook registration.

nodes.name: 05_notification_queue.sql
nodes.summary: Generic notification queue: creates notification_channel/status/priority enums, notification_templates, notification_queue, and notification_deliveries tables. Provides queue_notification(), fetch_pending_notifications(), mark_notification_sent(), schedule_notification_retry() SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
nodes.languageNotes: Priority-based notification scheduling with worker-safe SKIP LOCKED pattern.

nodes.name: 06_background_job_queue.sql
nodes.summary: Background job queue: creates job_queue table with job type, payload, status, priority, retry fields. Provides claim_jobs(), complete_job(), fail_job(), get_pending_jobs() SECURITY DEFINER RPCs for worker coordination.
nodes.languageNotes: Job claim pattern with lease-based concurrency control for distributed workers.

nodes.name: 07_settlement_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Settlement engine: creates payment_orders, payment_attempts, payment_ledger, refunds, and settlements tables with full financial audit trail. Provides create_payment_order(), record_payment_attempt(), settle_hospital_payments() SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.
nodes.languageNotes: Financial integrity with ledger entries for every monetary movement. Idempotent payment order creation.

nodes.name: 08_analytics_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Analytics engine: creates analytics tables for tracking booking metrics, queue performance, doctor productivity, and patient flow statistics.

nodes.name: 09_abuse_protection_&_rate_limiting.sql
nodes.summary: Abuse protection and rate limiting: creates rate_limit_config, rate_limit_logs, and api_request_logs tables. Implements per-hospital, per-endpoint rate limiting with configurable thresholds and logging.

nodes.name: 10_audit_&_security_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Audit and security engine: creates audit_events table for immutable audit trail. Provides log_audit_event() and helper functions for tracking all significant system mutations.

nodes.name: 11_realtime_presence_schedule_tasks.sql
nodes.summary: Realtime, presence, and scheduled tasks: configures Supabase Realtime for live updates, adds presence tracking, and scheduled task infrastructure.

nodes.name: 12_hospital_configuration_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Hospital configuration engine: creates configuration tables for per-hospital settings, preferences, and operational parameters.

nodes.name: 13_payment_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Payment engine: integrates Razorpay with payment_orders table, payment_attempts tracking, webhook handling for payment status updates, and refund processing.

nodes.name: 14_dead_letter_queue.sql
nodes.summary: Dead letter queue: creates dead_letter_jobs table for capturing failed jobs that exceeded retry limits, with retention and analysis capabilities.

nodes.name: 15_partitioning_strategy.sql
nodes.summary: Table partitioning strategy: implements range partitioning on time-series tables (bookings, audit_events) for scalability.

nodes.name: 16_idempotency_hardening.sql
nodes.summary: Idempotency hardening: adds idempotency_key columns and unique constraints to key mutation tables. Ensures safe retry behavior for all financial operations.

nodes.name: 17_queue_monitoring_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Queue monitoring engine: creates queue_metrics, queue_health_checks, and SLA monitoring tables for real-time queue performance tracking.

nodes.name: 18_config_versioning_&_rollback.sql

nodes.name: 19_background_worker_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Background worker engine v2: creates job_queue_v2, worker_registry, worker_leases, and worker_heartbeats tables. Provides claim_jobs_v2(), complete_job_v2(), register_worker(), send_worker_heartbeat() RPCs. Known regression: claim_jobs_v2 does not populate lease_expires_at.
nodes.languageNotes: Lease-based worker coordination replacing v1 claim pattern. Heartbeat mechanism for worker liveness.

nodes.name: 20_presence_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Presence engine: implements real-time presence tracking for active users, doctors, and queue participants.

nodes.name: 21_analytics_rollups.sql
nodes.summary: Analytics rollups: creates materialized views and rollup tables for pre-computed analytics metrics (hourly, daily, weekly aggregations).

nodes.name: 22_partition_automation.sql

nodes.name: 23_retention_&_cleanup_engine.sql

nodes.languageNotes: P0-04: booking_fee_inr has no runtime writer, only one-time backfill.

nodes.name: 30_device_sessions.sql

nodes.name: 31_doctor_leave_management.sql
nodes.summary: Doctor leave management: extends doctor_leaves table with approval workflow, leave type, and balance tracking.

nodes.name: 32_subscription_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Subscription engine: creates subscription_plans, hospital_subscriptions, and subscription_invoices tables for SaaS billing.

nodes.name: 33_settlement_engine_refactor.sql
nodes.summary: Settlement engine refactor: reorganizes settlement tables and RPCs for improved clarity and performance.

nodes.name: 34_payment_ledger_cleanup.sql
nodes.summary: Payment ledger cleanup: fixes data integrity issues in payment_ledger and ensures correct financial record state.

nodes.name: 35_hospital_config_enhancements.sql
nodes.summary: Hospital configuration enhancements: adds additional config fields and validation rules for hospital-level settings.

nodes.name: 36_audit_standardization.sql
nodes.summary: Audit standardization: standardizes audit event types, actor fields, and severity levels across the system.

nodes.name: 37_feature_flags.sql
nodes.summary: Feature flags: creates feature_flags table and is_feature_enabled() function for controlled feature rollouts.

nodes.name: 38_missing_rpc_functions.sql
nodes.summary: Missing RPC functions: backfills RPC functions that were referenced by code but not yet defined in migrations.

nodes.name: 39_schema_alignment.sql
nodes.summary: Schema alignment: aligns database schema with the generated TypeScript types, fixing drift between code and database.

nodes.name: 40_subscription_usage_engine.sql
nodes.summary: Subscription usage engine: creates usage_metrics and usage_limits tables for metered billing and quota enforcement.

nodes.name: 41_integration_hardening.sql
nodes.summary: Integration hardening: adds additional validation, security checks, and integrity constraints to integration tables.

nodes.name: 42_whatsapp_conversational_engine.sql
nodes.summary: WhatsApp conversational engine: creates conversation_state and handoff tables for stateful WhatsApp conversations with intent routing.

nodes.name: 43_queue_runtime.sql
nodes.summary: Queue runtime: the largest queue migration, implementing queue pause/resume, token skip/restore, doctor delay marking, recall, and emergency patient insertion as SQL RPCs.

nodes.name: 44_queue_runtime_flag.sql
nodes.summary: Queue runtime feature flag: small migration toggling queue_runtime feature flag for safe rollout.

nodes.name: 45_queue_operations.sql
nodes.summary: Queue operations: extends queue runtime with operations RPCs for batch processing, queue health evaluation, and admin notifications.

nodes.name: 46_doctor_clinical_operations.sql
nodes.summary: Doctor clinical operations: creates consultation_notes, prescriptions, and clinical_assessments tables. Provides clinical workflow RPCs for the doctor dashboard.

nodes.name: 47_enterprise_command_center.sql
nodes.summary: Enterprise command center: large migration creating executive dashboards, multi-hospital analytics, hospital comparison views, and command center RPCs.

nodes.name: 48_privilege_hardening.sql
nodes.summary: Privilege hardening: revokes PUBLIC grants on SECURITY DEFINER functions, establishes fail-closed privilege boundary. Known issue (F16-04): the PUBLIC grant is never revoked (only named-role grants are), and the supabase_admin grantor rows were silently skipped.
nodes.languageNotes: F16-04: fail-closed guarantee does not hold - PUBLIC grant is never revoked; supabase_admin grantor rows silently skipped when migration ran as postgres.

nodes.languageNotes: F16-04 mitigation: functions safe by accident due to CREATE OR REPLACE preserving prior ACL.

tour.title: Project Overview & Operating Contract
tour.description: Begin with ARCHITECTURE.md to learn SETURA's SQL-first design: all business logic lives in PostgreSQL (SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, triggers, constraints), while Deno edge functions are a thin HTTP orchestration layer. CLAUDE.md is the operating contract for anyone working in the repo: it defines the non-negotiables (security, multi-tenancy, financial correctness, auditability), the established architecture primitives, and the truth hierarchy. Read these two together to understand both what SETURA is and how to work in it.

tour.title: Database Foundation Migration
tour.description: Every SETURA feature builds on migration 01_foundation.sql, which runs first. It enables pgcrypto/uuid-ossp/pg_trgm/citext, defines the core enums (user_role_type, booking_status, booking_source), installs the set_updated_at() trigger helper, and — most importantly — the prevent_hospital_id_update() guard. This guard enforces multi-tenancy at the database level: hospital_id columns become effectively immutable. Understanding this file is a prerequisite for every later migration.

tour.title: Atomic Token & Booking Engine
tour.description: The booking engine (migration 02) introduces bookings, booking_events, queue_sessions, and hospital_daily_counters. The architectural centerpiece is atomic token allocation via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE RETURNING — the only safe way to allocate per-doctor daily tokens under concurrent load. Patient deduplication by (hospital_id, normalized_phone) is also enforced here. This migration is what makes 'booked → checked_in → waiting → called → in_consultation → completed' a state machine, not just a status string.

tour.title: Authentication, Authorization & Tenancy
tour.description: Every edge function in SETURA starts with auth.ts. resolveAuth() verifies the JWT via Supabase Auth, loads the profile, queries user_roles for hospital membership, and applies the role hierarchy (global_admin > hospital_admin > doctor > receptionist). requireRole() is the action-level guard, and requireHospitalAccess() enforces tenant isolation. Paired with errors.ts (18 SeturError subclasses), this pair is the security boundary — no edge function may bypass it, and no database RPC should be exposed without an equivalent check.
tour.languageLesson: ROLE_HIERARCHY is encoded as a numeric precedence in TypeScript so the highest-privilege role always wins across multiple user_roles rows. The withAuth wrapper composes resolveAuth + error handling so each handler is a single concern.

tour.title: API & Error Contracts
tour.description: Every endpoint returns the same JSON envelope defined in response.ts: { success, data, correlationId, timestamp }. handleErrorResponse is the outermost catch-block handler, turning any SeturError into a typed HTTP response with CORS headers. docs/API_CONTRACTS.md formalizes the request/response shape, the Idempotency-Key header convention, and the X-Hospital-ID header requirement. docs/ERROR_CONTRACT.md enumerates the error taxonomy — auth, booking, queue, idempotency, rate limit, infrastructure. Read these together to know what every endpoint must look like on the wire.

tour.title: Idempotency, Audit & Privilege Hardening
tour.description: Three non-negotiable safety layers. idempotency.ts implements the withIdempotency wrapper around the api_idempotency_keys table so a retried POST returns the original response instead of double-mutating. audit.ts exposes logAuditEvent which writes to the trigger-enforced append-only audit_logs — UPDATE and DELETE are rejected at the database level. Migration 48_privilege_hardening.sql documents the F16-04 caveat: a new or resignatured SECURITY DEFINER function does not automatically lose its PUBLIC grant, so each one needs its own explicit REVOKE.
tour.languageLesson: Idempotency in SETURA is two-layered: the api_idempotency_keys registry stores response payloads for HTTP replay, while the bookings/payments tables carry unique-constraint idempotency keys as a backstop. Both must be in place to handle retries, double-clicks, and webhook redeliveries safely.

tour.title: Edge Runtime: Booking Creation
tour.description: create-booking/index.ts is the canonical example of the full SETURA edge pipeline (documented in the file header as 16 numbered steps). It runs: CORS preflight, idempotency claim, JWT+role+hospital validation, zod body parsing, rate limit (phone+IP), hospital open/holiday rules, doctor availability, queue capacity, phone blocklist, find-or-create patient, atomic token allocation, WhatsApp confirmation enqueue, notification enqueue, audit log, idempotency completion, typed response. Every other mutating edge function in the repo is a variation of this pattern — study it once, reuse it everywhere.

tour.title: Edge Runtime: Live Queue Control
tour.description: queue-control/index.ts is the live-queue API for receptionists and doctors. Its ten actions — pause, resume, recall, skip, restore, mark_absent, call, delay, clear_delay, snapshot — all run through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that enforce one-active-consultation-per-doctor and append to queue_runtime_events (migration 43). Every action is idempotent via deterministic keys, so a double-tap or network retry is safe. This is also the read path for queue displays and the write path for analytics rollups.

tour.title: Edge Runtime: Payment & Settlement Engines
tour.description: Money flows are split across two engines. create-payment-order/index.ts integrates Razorpay: it creates a payment_orders row, calls Razorpay's Orders API, and returns the short_id the patient pays against (migration 13_payment_engine.sql). settlement-engine/index.ts is the financial close: it computes hospital_settlements + settlement_items from platform fees and exposes snapshot endpoints for finance dashboards (migration 07_settlement_engine.sql). Together they bridge an external PSP and the append-only financial_ledger, which the daily_collection_entries table materializes for every dashboard and report.

tour.title: WhatsApp Conversation Engine
tour.description: WhatsApp is a first-class patient channel. Inbound flow: process-whatsapp-webhook verifies the Meta HMAC signature, deduplicates via webhook_events, and hands the message to whatsapp_conversation_engine.ts, which loads/updates whatsapp_conversation_states (migration 42) and routes through the deterministic intent router — no LLM, only keyword matching with explicit handoff on ambiguity. Each intent dispatches to a flow module (book/cancel/reschedule/queue/handoff), which delegates the actual mutation to the canonical booking/cancel RPCs — never duplicating business logic. Outbound flow: send-whatsapp-message is invoked by the background worker, calls the Meta Cloud API, writes delivery logs, and retries with DLQ on exhaustion.

tour.title: Background Worker & Cron
tour.description: Off-thread work in SETURA is job-based, not timer-based per task. run-background-worker/index.ts uses claim_jobs_v2 with SKIP LOCKED to atomically lease work, heartbeat to worker_heartbeat_log, and route to a payload handler; failures retry with backoff and ultimately land in dead_letter_jobs. run-cron-minute/index.ts is the per-minute orchestrator that enqueues reminder, rollup, health-check, and partition-automation jobs (requires CRON_SECRET). The shared worker.ts module owns the lease/heartbeat/retry primitives reused by every processor. Note: as of Phase 1.6, no scheduler is installed locally (P0-02), so this layer is testable but not yet self-driving.

tour.title: Test Suite, Commands & Local Operations
tour.description: SETURA tests run against the real local Supabase stack — no mocks for database or RPC behavior. The privilege_isolation.test.ts proves the SECURITY DEFINER boundary by asserting SQLSTATE 42501 (not 401) for anon/authenticated callers; whatsapp_conversational.test.ts exercises the full intent-to-delegation path; refund_sync.test.ts verifies process-refund keeps financial_ledger and daily_collection_entries consistent. deno.json defines the 10 authoritative tasks (validate:migrations, test, test:integration, gen:types:check, etc.) and .env.example lists the 21 placeholders (CRON_SECRET, WORKER_SECRET, META_APP_SECRET, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET, etc.) — no .env exists in the repo, so local runs need clearly-fake values, never real secrets.
tour.languageLesson: Deno tasks replace npm scripts entirely: there is no package.json, Makefile, or justfile. fmt and gen:types rewrite files and are never run casually — only check variants (fmt:check, gen:types:check) are read-only and safe for CI.
